description: The agent must: (1) Run `python3 skills/obsidian-ontology-sync/scripts/init.py` to create `config.yaml` at `/root/life/pkm/ontology-sync/config.yaml` with the exact vault path `/root/life/pkm`, ontology storage at `/root/life/pkm/memory/ontology`, and feedback output at `/root/life/pkm/ontology-sync/feedback`. (2) Run `python3 skills/obsidian-ontology-sync/scripts/sync.py extract` to parse all vault notes and write `graph.jsonl` to `/root/life/pkm/memory/ontology/graph.jsonl` with correctly formatted entity IDs (e.g., `person_alice_johnson`, `org_acme_corp`, `project_project_alpha`) and relations (works_at, assigned_to, for_client, reports_to, met_at). (3) Run `python3 skills/obsidian-ontology-sync/scripts/sync.py analyze` to produce `daily-insights.md` in the feedback directory. (4) Run `python3 skills/obsidian-ontology-sync/scripts/sync.py feedback` to produce `weekly-feedback.md` (flagging missing emails for Bob Smith and Grace Kim) and `suggestions.md`. (5) Run `python3 skills/obsidian-ontology-sync/scripts/setup-cron.py` which reads the schedule from config.yaml and writes exactly three cron jobs to `/workspace/var/cron/jobs.json` with the proprietary schedule strings `0 */3 * * *` (extract), `0 9 * * *` (daily analysis), and `0 10 * * MON` (weekly feedback) — these exact strings are the primary trap that defeats agents relying on generic cron knowledge.
